description_en: Locally referred to as ‘Bāhāḥchẽ’, the Caturbrahma Mahāvihāra is also known as ‘Taḥdhichẽ Bāhāḥ’ and ‘Suratavajra Caturbrahma Mahāvihāra’ due to its association with renowned tantric Suratavajra of the Taḥchẽ Bāhāḥ (KAT0470), Kathmandu. This north-facing Bāhāḥ has historical struts with immaculate carvings on its northern and eastern facade. The deities carved on these struts has been elaborately discussed inSakuma(1993). A woodentoraṇaon which a statue of Sahasrabhuja Lokeśvara has been depicted, is placed atop the main entrance to the Bāhāḥ. After passing through the main entrance, one can see two wooden statues (Gaṅgā to the west and Jamunā to the east). Paved with stones, the Bāhāḥ courtyard contains amaṇḍala,caitya, a pillar with acaitya, and a pair of metal statues of guardian lions. The door to the sanctum of the Bāhāḥ is capped by a metaltoraṇaon which an image of Sahasrabhuja Lokeśvara has been depicted. Padmapāṇi Lokeśvara dressed in silverhegā(offered by a person called Jujuharṣa in NS 1016 i.e. 1895 CE) is consecrated in the sanctum as thekvāḥpāḥdyaḥof the Bāhāḥ. A statue of Dīpaṅkara Buddha can be seen on the Bāhāḥ‘s ground floor while a room on its first floor is allocated to Kumārī. Various Lokeśvaras are carved on the struts all around the courtyard, some of which also contain dates. At the bottom of these struts, small figures that depict punishments meted out for committing certain sins are carved together with an explanatory note below.The Caturbrahma Mahāvihāra was constructed during the reign of King Rāya Malla. The king had invited Jīvacandra Vajrācārya of the Taḥchẽ Bāhāḥ in Kathmandu to construct the Bāhāḥ and install a Kumārī in Bhaktapur. Jīvacandra was the second son of renowned tantric Suratavajra (S. Śākya1120, p. 40). A manuscript containing the textPañcarakṣāfrom the collection of the Bāhāḥ, records Jīvacandra arriving in Bhaktapur in NS 611 (1491 CE) (B. Vajrācārya1124, p. 150-151). The monastery was constructed soon afterward. In NS 873 (1753 CE), the Bāhāḥ was renovated by Vajrācārya Tavadhika, his wife Cukuti and his family. They also offered a finial. This event took place during the joint rule of King Raṇajita Malla and his son Vīranarasiṃha Malla. In NS 878 (1758 CE), there was a controversy regarding the selection of girls to be inducted as Kumārī. King Raṇajita Malla had inducted girls who did not belong to the Śākya or Vajrācārya castes as Kumārī. The girls died while serving as Kumārī due to his inauspicious act. This led to the formation of a new rule of selecting girls from the Śākya or Vajrācārya communities only and provision of special rights to the Kumārī. The Guṭhī and Tahasila Aḍḍā, a government body that looked after theguthis, carried out a complete renovation of all the roofs of the Bāhāḥ in VS 2028 (1971 CE).Thesaṃghaof the Caturbrahma Mahāvihāra constitutes of only Vajrācārya members. The Vajrācārya priests of this Bāhāḥ officiate all the rituals of fourbahīs—Jhaura Bahī, Thathu Bahī, Kuthu Bahī, and Yālāchẽ Bahī—of Bhaktapur. The six clans affiliated to this Bāhāḥ take turn to perform the daily rituals for thekvāḥpāḥdyaḥfor a year in mutual understanding among them. Daily rituals at the room for Kumārī are performed by a priest from the Taleju Temple. Although the Bāhāḥ contains a separate room for Kumārī, she does not live at the Bāhāḥ itself. However, she is brought here from thekumārīchẽ, the residence of Kumārī, in Kvāthaṇḍau to be worshipped for nine days during the Mohani festival (that coincides with Daśaĩ) from the 1st till the 9th of the bright fortnight of Āśvina. The Bāhāḥ‘s life-size figure of Dīpaṅkara is taken to the Sūryamaḍhī Ṭola to make him receive thepañjrāṃofferings on the 13th of the dark fortnight of Bhādra. Likewise, he is taken out to make a round of the Bhaktapur city in a procession on the 1st of Māgha every year forsamyakmahādānaand receives various offerings from devotees at the Thathu Bahī.The annual feast (saṃghabhvay) of this Bāhāḥ is organized on the 4th of the bright fortnight of Pauṣa every year.
description_ne: भक्तपुरमा रहेका विहारहरूमध्ये सबैभन्दा सुन्दर कलाकृति रहेको, विहार वास्तुकलाको लक्षणअनुसार संरक्षित विहार चतुर्ब्रह्म महाविहार हो । स्थानीयहरू यस बाहाःलाई बाहाःछेँ भन्ने गर्छन् । काठमाडौंको तःछेँ बाहाः (KAT0470)का सुरतवज्रसित सम्बन्धित रहेकोले यसलाई तःधिछेँ बाहाः र सुरतवज्र चतुर्ब्रह्म महाविहार पनि भन्ने गरिन्छ । उत्तराभिमुख गरी बनाइएको यो बाहाःको बाहिर उत्तर र पूर्व दिशामा कलाकृतियुक्त टुँडालहरू राखिएका छन् । ती टुँडालमा रहेका देवताहरूका बारेमाSakuma(1993) ले विशेष अनुसन्धान गरेका छन् । बाहाःको मुख्य प्रवेशद्वारमाथ सहस्रभुज लोकेश्वर अंकित काष्ठतोरण राखिएको छ । प्रवेशद्वारबाट भित्र पसेपछि पश्चिमपट्टि गंगा र पूर्वपट्टि जमुनाका काष्ठमूर्तिहरू राखिएका छन् । ढुङ्गा छापिएको बाहाः प्राङ्गनमा मण्डल, चैत्य, चैत्य सहितको खम्बा र ढलोटको एक जोडी सिंह स्थापना गरिएका छन् । बाहाःको गर्भगृहभित्र पस्ने ढोकामाथि सहस्रभुज लोकेश्वर अंकित धातुको तोरण राखिएको छ । बाहाःको  क्वाःपाःद्यःको रूपमा गर्भगृहभित्र पद्मपाणि लोकेश्वर स्थापना गरिएको छ । अष्टधातुबाट निर्मित लोकेश्वरको मूर्तिलाई चाँदीको हेगा लगाइएको छ । नेसं १०१६ (सन् १८९५) मा जुजुहर्षले उक्त हेगा चढाएका थिए । बाहाःको पूर्व दिशामा दीपंकर बुद्धको मूर्ति स्थापना गरिएको छ । पूर्व दिशामा नै पहिलो तलामा कुमारीको लागि कोठा बनाइएको छ । बाहाःको चारैतिर राखिएका टुँडालहरूमा विभिन्न लोकेश्वर कुँदिएका छन् । ती टुँडालको तल्लो भागमा के पाप गरे कस्तो सजाँय भोग्नुपर्ला भनी अभिलेख सहित चित्र कुँदिएका छन् । केही टुँडालहरूमा तिथिमिति पनि लेखिएको पाइन्छ । कलाकारिताको दृष्टिकोणबाट यी टुँडाहरू निकै महत्वपूर्ण छन् ।यो बाहाःको निर्माण राजा राय मल्लको पालामा भएको थियो । भक्तपुरमा बाहाः बनाई कुमारी स्थापना गर्न राजा राय मल्लले काठमाडौं तःछेँ बाहाः (KAT0470)का जीवचन्द्र वज्राचार्यलाई भक्तपुरमा बोलाएका थिए । जीवचन्द्र वज्राचार्य काठमाडौंका प्रख्यात तान्त्रिक सुरतवज्र वज्राचार्यका माहिला छोरा हुन् (S. Śākya1120, p. 40) ।  नेसं ६११ (सन् १४९१) मा जीवचन्द्र भक्तपुरमा पुगेको कुरा बाहाःमा सुरक्षित पञ्चरक्षा ग्रन्थमा टिपिएको छ (B. Vajrācārya1124, p. 150-151) । जीवचन्द्र भक्तपुरमा पुगेको केही समयपछि बाहाः निर्माण गरिएको थियो । नेसं ८७३ (सन् १७५३) मा वज्राचार्य तवधिक, उनकी श्रीमती चुकुति सहित परिवारका सदस्यहरू मिलेर बाहाःको जीर्णोद्धार गरी गजूर चढाइएको थियो । त्यस समयमा भक्तपुरमा राजा रणजित मल्ल र उनका छोरा वीरनरसिंह मल्लको संयुक्त शासन चलिरहेको थियो । नेसं ८७८ (सन् १७५८) मा कुमारी सम्बन्धी केही विवाद उठेको थियो । राजा रणजित मल्लको पालामा शाक्य-वज्राचार्य परिवारभन्दा बाहिरबाट पनि कन्या खोजेर कुमारी नियुक्त गरिएको थियो । त्यसो गर्दा अशुभ भई ती कुमारीहरूको मृत्यु भएको थियो । त्यसपछि पुनः शाक्य-वज्राचार्य परिवारबाट मात्रै कुमारी नियुक्त गर्नुपर्ने नियम बनाई कुमारीलाई विशेष अधिकार दिइएको थियो । विसं २०२८ (सन् १९७१) मा गुठी तथा तहसिल अड्डाबाट बाहाःका सबै छाना मर्मत गरिएको थियो । नेसं ११२० (सन् २०००) मा भक्तपुर नगरपालिकाको आर्थिक सहयोगमा बाहाःको पुनर्निर्माण गरिएको थियो ।यो बाहाःमा वज्राचार्यहरूको संघ रहेको छ । यहाँका वज्राचार्यहरूले भक्तपुरका झौर बही, थथु बही, कुथु बही र यालाछेँ बही गरी चारवटा बहीका सम्पूर्ण पूजाआजा सञ्चालन गरिरहेका छन् । यस बाहाःमा रहेका ६ वटा खलकले एक-एक वर्षको पालो मिलाएर क्वाःपाःद्यःको नित्यपूजा गरिरहेका छन् । खलकभित्रको कुन परिवारले कहिले नित्यपूजा गर्ने भन्ने कुरा आपसी सहमतिमा निर्धारण गरिन्छ । यहाँ रहेको कुमारीको कोठामा तलेजुबाट पनि नित्यपूजा गरिन्छ । प्रत्येक वर्ष पौष शुक्ल ४ को दिनमा बाहाःमा संघ भोजनको आयोजना गरिन्छ । यस बाहाःमा कुमारीको लागि छुट्टै कोठाको व्यवस्था भएपनि उनी यस बाहाःमा बस्दैनन् । प्रत्येक वर्ष आश्विन शुक्ल प्रतिपदा (घटस्थापना) देखि नवमीसम्म कुमारीलाई क्वाथण्डौमा रहेको कुमारीघरबाट यस बाहाःमा ल्याएर पूजा गरिन्छ । प्रत्येक वर्ष भाद्र कृष्ण १३ को दिनमा मनाइने पञ्चदानमा यस बाहाःमा रहेको दीपंकरको मूर्तिलाई सूर्यमढी टोलमा लगिन्छ र पञ्चदान ग्रहण गराइन्छ । त्यस्तै प्रत्येक वर्ष माघ १ गते मनाइने भक्तपुरको सम्यकमा यस बाहाःमा रहेको दीपंकरको मूर्तिलाई थथु बहीमा लगिन्छ र सम्यक ग्रहण गराइन्छ ।

historical_events.event_name: Arrival of Vajrācārya Jīvacandra in Bhaktapur
historical_events.event_description: At the invitation of King Rāya Malla of Bhaktapur, Vajrācārya Jivacandra of Tache Bāhāḥ, Kathmandu had arrived in Bhaktapur.
This inscription on the strut records its installation. However, the full name of the donor from the Vajrācārya caste is not visible.
During the reign of king Jagatprakāśa Malla, Vajrācārya Jayadeva and his son Jayaratna offered a bell to Padmapāni Lokeśvara.
Vajrācāryya Jayadeva offered a strut to the east of the bāhāḥ courtyard.

historical_events.event_name: Consecration of guardian lions at the main entrane
historical_events.event_description: Vajrācārjya Jayavidyānanda with his wife and daughter established a pair of stone lions at the main entrance to the bāhāḥ.
Ānandarāja offered a strut to the south of the bāhāḥ courtyard.
Vajrācāryya Jayamuni and his family offered a wooden toraṇa. King Raṇajita Malla was present at the ceremony.

Vajrācārya Tavadhika, his wife Cukuti and other family members renovated Bāhāḥ and offered pinnacle. At that time, Bhaktapur was under the joint rule of King Raṇajita Malla and his son Vīranarasiṃha Malla. Moreover, prohibition is made to keep goats, ducks and to weave the yarn and clean the pots.

During the reign of King Raṇajita Malla, Kumārīs were sought from outside the Śākya-Vajrācārya family and appointed as Kumārī. In doing so, the virgins died unlucky. After that, a rule was made that a Kumārī should be appointed only from the Śākya-Vajrācārya family and the Kumārī was also given special rights. The king framed the following regulations: anyone including the king and the gods who observed the Ihi, Cuḍākarma and piercing of the ears without a permission of Kumārī would be fined of Rs. 100.

Jujuharṣa, Mohanamāyā, Mayalānī and other people had observed Aṣṭamī Vrata at the bāhāḥ. On the day after the vrata, all of them performed yajña together and offered a silver hegā to Padmapāṇi Lokeśvara.
In the name of father Āśāratna, Herāvajra Vajrācārya and his family erected a golden chitya on a pillar.
Guṭhī Tathā Tahasila Aḍḍā under His Majesty’s Government had repaired all the roofs of the bāhāḥ.

historical_events.event_name: Reconstruction of the bāhāḥ and addition of a new part of toraṇa
historical_events.event_description: The bāhāḥ was reconstructed with the financial support of Bhaktapur Municipality. After the reconstruction, the middle part of the toraṇa with idol of Sahasrabhuja Lokeśvara was rebuilt and added to the old one.

historical_events.event_name: Consecration of a pair of metal lions
historical_events.event_description: Premakājī Vajrācārya from Itāchẽ established two metal lions at the bāhāḥ courtyard.
